set.approach: Two long backcountry approaches reach the dome. From the west, take the Bubbs Creek trail up from Cedar Grove, then turn north onto a faint use trail on the west side of Charlotte Creek and climb to the base. From the east, cross Kearsarge Pass from Onion Valley, drop to Charlotte Lake, then continue down to the foot of the dome. Camps in the forest near the base are pleasant, and bear canisters are required on both approaches. The route starts in an obvious bowl on the south side, a short way right of the South Face route.
set.descent_text: The top of the route eases to third-class ground along the summit ridge. Do not start down right away: traverse north along the ridge a long way, past an exposed stretch that then eases, and head for the low point of the north ridge before scrambling down from there.

review.notes: Approach: dome area page. Start: route page. Descent: route page (traverse north) and South Face page (north ridge to its low point).

set.approach: Two long backcountry approaches reach the dome. From the west, take the Bubbs Creek trail up from Cedar Grove, then turn north onto a faint use trail on the west side of Charlotte Creek and climb to the base. From the east, cross Kearsarge Pass from Onion Valley, drop to Charlotte Lake, then continue down to the foot of the dome. The route starts on the south face, under the large roof on the right-hand side of the dome, beside Against the Grain.
set.descent_text: From the top of the last pitch, scramble to the summit and take the usual third- and fourth-class walk-off. That descent follows the north ridge to its lowest point, then scrambles down.

review.notes: Approach: area page; start from route page. Descent: route page names the standard walk-off; South Face page gives its line.

set.approach: Two long backcountry approaches reach the dome. From the west, take the Bubbs Creek trail up from Cedar Grove, then turn north onto a faint use trail on the west side of Charlotte Creek and climb to the base. From the east, cross Kearsarge Pass from Onion Valley, drop to Charlotte Lake, then continue down to the foot of the dome. Camps in the forest near the base are pleasant, and bear canisters are required on both approaches. The line begins on a fourth-class hand crack of gentle angle that trends rightward toward the biggest roof on the southeast face.
set.descent_text: Parties who would rather not carry shoes and extra gear to the top can rappel the route itself with a pair of ropes.

review.notes: Approach: area page; start from route page. Rappelling the route is stated on the route page; no walk-off is stated for this line.

set.approach: From Onion Valley, cross Kearsarge Pass, drop to Charlotte Lake, and continue down to the foot of the dome, which is a quicker way to reach this line than the western approach from Cedar Grove. The route is on the far right side of the east face. It starts directly below the long left-facing corner in the middle of that face, near the single pine growing there.
set.descent_text: The line ends on the dome and parties walk off. Seen from the east, the walk-off follows the right-hand skyline to a notch, then drops down a curving gully past a stand of trees.

review.notes: Approach and start: area and route pages. Walk-off: route page says walk off; photo caption gives the line from the east.

set.approach: The approach from the Gem Lakes trailhead runs to the Thousand Island Lakes basin, which makes a good camp (mosquitoes can be thick in early summer). From camp, ascend the snowfield up to the shoulder under the climb and transition to the rock there; an ice axe is needed on the snow, and crampons if it is frozen hard.
set.descent_text: Head down toward the saddle separating Banner from Ritter, where both sides hold snow, so carry an ice axe. From the saddle, glissade the snow slope below it back toward the lakes.

review.notes: Approach and saddle descent from the route page; the area page independently says the descent is through the Ritter-Banner saddle with snow both sides.

set.approach: Park at the end of Pine Creek Road at the pack station and walk through the gate onto the Pine Creek trail. Follow it as far as the junction signed for Granite Park and Honeymoon Lake, go around Honeymoon Lake, and continue up the drainage. Leave the trail and travel cross-country to a camp near Golden Lake. The route starts left of the toe of the northeast ridge, left of an orange right-facing corner.
set.descent_text: Descend the west slope of the peak and return through Royce Col.

review.notes: Approach: area page. Start and descent: route page.

set.approach: Park at the end of Pine Creek Road at the pack station and walk through the gate onto the Pine Creek trail. Follow it as far as the junction signed for Granite Park and Honeymoon Lake, go around Honeymoon Lake, and continue up the drainage. Leave the trail and travel cross-country to a camp near Golden Lake. On the north side of the peak, work out the most direct line through the talus to the base. The start is marked by an obvious triangular roof that forms a small alcove a short way up the first pitch.

review.notes: Approach: area page; base from route page. No descent stated; skipped.

set.approach: Park at the end of Pine Creek Road at the pack station and walk through the gate onto the Pine Creek trail. Follow it as far as the junction signed for Granite Park and Honeymoon Lake, go around Honeymoon Lake, and continue up the drainage. Leave the trail and travel cross-country to a camp near Golden Lake. This is a start variation to Treasure Hunt. Aim for the large triangular roof above the snowfield, which sits to the west of Treasure Hunt's first pitch.

review.notes: Approach: area page; start from route page. No descent stated; skipped.

set.approach: From the Onion Valley parking loop, take the trail that splits from the Kearsarge Pass trail and runs north into the basins holding Golden Trout Lake and the Dragon Peak lakes. Pass the waterfall on its right, cross the creek where the trail does, and climb to a meadow with large towers to the north. Camping is at the two lakes under the peak. At the last lake, aim for the chute on the climbers' right (north) side of the peak, not the south chute used by the scramble route. The climb starts in the big dihedral and chimney system reached from the col between Dragon Peak and Dragon's Tooth.

review.notes: Approach from the area and route pages. No descent stated for this route; skipped.

set.approach: Take the approach to Budd Lake that is used for Cathedral Peak and Matthes Crest, then continue over Echo Pass into the Echo Peaks. The route is on the southwest face of Peak 9, which starts up a low-angle ramp with many ledges for belays.
set.descent_text: From the summit, make a short rappel from the anchor on top (a bolt plus a fixed piece) to the ledge below. Then descend the chasm that separates Peaks 8 and 9 with a short fourth-class downclimb back to the base.

review.notes: All from the route page; area page confirms the Budd Lake approach.

set.approach: Hike the High Sierra Trail to the Hamilton Lake camp, with bear boxes at several camps on the way. From the upper camp, follow the trail east toward Precipice Lake up the switchbacks. After a short stretch you reach a big cliff with a roof where the trail cuts back east; walk just past the overhang and cut up some loose third-class ground, or go on to where the switchbacks end and climb a bushy gully, then scramble left toward the dome. There is no set trail to the base, but heading for the dome works. The route climbs the south face and southwest buttress.
set.descent_text: From the summit, drop down the back side on third-class ground for a short distance. Continue east down the ridge to slabs or a gully that leads back to your packs. A stream runs here in early season and after thunderstorms.

review.notes: Area page gives approach and descent; the route page mentions a back-side scramble from the summit.

set.approach: Follow the approach to the Daff area and the West Crack, then continue northwest to Doda Dome and walk around to its west face. The route is the conspicuous right-facing corner high on the west face that rises from a ledge.
set.descent_text: Walk off from the top of the corner.

review.notes: Approach: area page; the corner and walk-off from the route page.

set.approach: The quickest way to the north and east sides of the peak is from the Bishop Pass trail at Long Lake. Cross the outlet of the lake, then either stay left and hike, or climb the solid ramps and slabs. The route follows the rock rib that separates the towers of the east face from the northeast ridge, starting up a diagonal ramp just right of the steep towers, about a hundred yards left of the left black streak.

review.notes: Approach path from the approach-trail page; start from the route page. No descent stated; skipped.

set.approach: From Twin Lakes, follow the Horse Creek trail toward Horse Creek Pass. Near the peak, leave the trail and pick a path across a short but rough moraine to the base of the north buttress, which is plainly visible from the trail on the way up.

review.notes: Area page only. The route page found by search belongs to a different peak and was not used. No descent stated for the buttress; skipped.

set.approach: Park at Twin Lakes near Bridgeport, then walk through the campground to the south side of the meadow at its back and cross Robinson Creek on a log bridge. Take the dirt road to a single-track, then climb the hillside well east of Horse Creek, following game trails and use trails on the east side of Blacksmith Creek. There is no maintained trail, so expect casual sidehilling and some thick brush. Pass the cliffs and talus fields, then cross to the west side of the creek where it enters a canyon, and continue to Glacier Lake, where there are good bivy spots at the southwest corner. A wilderness permit is required for overnight trips, and bear canisters are required.

review.notes: Area page only (approach to the lake below the peak). No route-level descent; skipped.

set.approach: The most direct approach is up Rafferty Canyon from Tuolumne Meadows; the other is from Lyell Canyon on the John Muir Trail, which is longer. Either way, you reach the Vogelsang High Sierra Camp at the foot of the peak. Take the trail from the camp toward Vogelsang Lake. About halfway up, the trail passes close to a big slab on the west side of the peak broken by many vertical cracks; the buttress above that slab is where the route climbs.

review.notes: Area page for the approach and camp; route page for the slab. No descent stated; skipped.

set.descent_text: From the summit, walk and scramble off the west side of the formation until you reach sandy scree. Continue down one of the first gullies on the west or south side of the formation.

review.notes: Route page only; no approach read.

set.approach: Start at the Horton Lakes trailhead, reached by a four-wheel-drive road from Buttermilk Road. The route begins at the toe of the northeast ridge of Basin Mountain, reached by a long climb up the sagebrush slope from the trailhead. The lower ridge has a series of towers, some best climbed over and others bypassed, with complicated route-finding.

review.notes: Approach from area and route pages. Descent from the route page is too vague; skipped.
